claim.pdf_says: "D.31.2   Temporal format ACCEPT statement" is printed at the same typographic rank as "D.31.1   General" (page 1192) - both are third-level clause headings under "D.31 Date and time handling".
claim.markdown_says: ## D.31.2 Temporal format ACCEPT statement   (while its sibling on page 1192 is "### D.31.1 General", and their common parent is "## D.31 Date and time handling")
claim.why_it_matters: D.31.2 is rendered as a sibling of its own parent D.31 rather than as a child, and as a peer of neither. Sibling headings at different levels break the document outline, so any TOC generated from this file, and any tooling that resolves "the enclosing clause" for a citation, mis-parents everything from D.31.2 onward.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on three independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind label is flatly wrong. The heading is present, verbatim, in the correct position: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48175 reads '## D.31.2 Temporal format ACCEPT statement', immediately after the two numbered list items that close D.31.1 and immediately before '### D.31.2.1 General' - exactly the printed order on the page. The clause number, the title text, and the anchor '' are all correct. No word of PDF content is absent, altered, reordered, or added. The only thing at issue is the count of '#' characters, which is a markdown formatting attribute, not PDF content. (2) THE CLAIM'S PDF PREMISE IS VACUOUS - I measured the printed glyphs. Extracting span metrics from the canonical PDF (fitz page index 1192 = printed 1163) shows EVERY heading on the page is Cambria,Bold at size 11.67 pt at left margin x=80.0: 'D.31.2 Temporal format ACCEPT statement' (y=279.9), 'D.31.2.1 General' (y=305.2), 'D.31.2.2 ACCEPT FROM DATE' (y=368.4), 'D.31.2.3 ...' (y=444.3), 'D.31.2.4 ...' (y=507.5), 'D.31.2.5 ...' (y=583.4). The preceding page (fitz index 1191 = printed 1162) is identical: 'D.29 CALL-CONVENTION directive' (y=90.2), 'D.30 ENTRY-CONVENTION clause' (y=341.2), 'D.31 Date and time handling' (y=503.6) and 'D.31.1 General' (y=527.9) are ALL Cambria,Bold 11.67 pt at x=63.5, and I confirmed this visually in the 300 dpi renders of both pages. So ISO prints the depth-1 clause D.31 at precisely the SAME typographic rank as the depth-2 clause D.31.1 and the depth-3 clause D.31.2.1. Annex D carries ZERO typographic rank information - hierarchy is conveyed exclusively by the dotted clause number. The claim's observation that D.31.2 'is printed at the same typographic rank as D.31.1' is therefore true but proves nothing: D.31.2 is also printed at the same typographic rank as its own parent D.31, as its own child D.31.2.1, and as D.29. No markdown heading depth can contradict a source that encodes no depth, and the depth the source DOES encode - the clause number - is transcribed correctly. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE ARGUMENT DOES NOT HOLD. (a) The transcription's raw heading depth is already not a tree by construction: the page-break markers are themselves headings ('## Page 1193' at line 48172, and page 1194 opens with '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at level 1), so they interleave with and outrank content headings throughout. Any TOC built from raw '#' depth was already meaningless before D.31.2 and remains so after; consumers must key on the clause number, which is intact. (b) Citation parent-resolution runs off the clause number ('D.31.2.4' -> 'D.31.2' -> 'D.31'), which is unambiguous and present in both the heading text and the anchor id. (c) The claim that this 'mis-parents everything from D.31.2 onward' is false on inspection: the very next heading, line 48178, returns to '### D.31.2.1 General', and D.31.2.2 through D.31.2.5 are all '###'. Nothing downstream is re-parented; the marker merely oscillates for one line. Finally, this is a global transcription artifact, not a page-1193 event. The same '##'-where-a-sibling-is-'###' oscillation recurs across the whole annex - D.31.2.6 and D.31.2.7 (lines 48210, 48215), D.31.3.3 through D.31.3.9 (48255-48285), D.31.5.2 and D.31.5.3 through D.31.5.11 (48344-48435) are all '##' while their own siblings D.31.3.1/D.31.3.2 and D.31.5.1 are '###'. Flagging one instance of a document-wide depth-assignment artifact as a page-1193 'missing heading' with structural severity is a false positive. If the level oscillation is to be normalized at all, it is a one-time mechanical pass over the whole file driven by clause-number depth, not a per-page reconciliation finding - and it changes no meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: No discrepancy. The heading '## D.31.2 Temporal format ACCEPT statement' is present verbatim and correctly positioned; nothing is missing, so 'missing-heading' misdescribes it. The PDF prints every Annex D heading - D.29, D.30, D.31, D.31.1, D.31.2, D.31.2.1 through D.31.2.5 - in identical Cambria Bold at 11.67 pt at an identical left margin, so the printed page asserts no typographic hierarchy at all and cannot be contradicted by a markdown heading depth; the hierarchy it does encode, the dotted clause number, is transcribed correctly. The '##' vs '###' inconsistency is a real but purely cosmetic, document-wide depth-assignment artifact of the transcription (recurring at D.31.2.6, D.31.2.7, D.31.3.3-D.31.3.9, D.31.5.2-D.31.5.11 and elsewhere), it does not propagate past the single line because D.31.2.1 immediately resumes '###', and it is moot for outline purposes because the page-marker headings ('## Page 1193', '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)') already outrank and interleave with content headings by design.
